name: mapreduce
description: MapReduce word-count benchmark: generate text, split into N batches, N parallel mappers, shuffle/flatten, M parallel reducers (N=3, W=5000, M=5).

nodes.name: generate_text
nodes.description: Dataset generation (entry step, no inputs). Generate the input text of W=5000 total words from the vocabulary [cat, dog, bird, horse, pig], each distributed evenly and shuffled randomly (so M=5 different words, 1000 occurrences each). W and the vocabulary are parameters (defaults W=5000, vocabulary [cat, dog, bird, horse, pig]; optional integer seed param, default unset = non-deterministic shuffle). When W is not divisible by the vocabulary size, distribute the remainder one extra occurrence to the first words so the total is exactly W. Write a single plain-text file of whitespace-separated words (single spaces, one line). This is the only step allowed to be specific to this vocabulary.

outputs.name: input_text.txt
outputs.description: W whitespace-separated words, evenly distributed over the vocabulary and randomly shuffled

nodes.code:
"""Generate the MapReduce word-count input text.

W total words drawn evenly from a vocabulary (default [cat, dog, bird, horse, pig]),
randomly shuffled, written as one line of single-space-separated words.
"""

import random

DEFAULT_W = 5000
DEFAULT_VOCABULARY = ["cat", "dog", "bird", "horse", "pig"]


def main(inputs: dict, outputs: dict, params: dict) -> None:
    total_words = int(params.get("W", DEFAULT_W))
    vocabulary = list(params.get("vocabulary", DEFAULT_VOCABULARY))
    seed = params.get("seed")

    if total_words <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"W must be a positive integer, got {total_words}")
    if not vocabulary:
        raise ValueError("vocabulary must contain at least one word")
    if len(set(vocabulary)) != len(vocabulary):
        raise ValueError(f"vocabulary contains duplicate words: {vocabulary}")
    for word in vocabulary:
        if not isinstance(word, str) or not word or any(c.isspace() for c in word):
            raise ValueError(f"vocabulary word must be a non-empty string without whitespace: {word!r}")

    base, remainder = divmod(total_words, len(vocabulary))
    words = []
    for i, word in enumerate(vocabulary):
        count = base + (1 if i < remainder else 0)
        words.extend([word] * count)

    rng = random.Random(int(seed)) if seed is not None else random.Random()
    rng.shuffle(words)

    if len(words) != total_words:
        raise RuntimeError(f"generated {len(words)} words, expected {total_words}")

    with open(outputs["output1"], "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(" ".join(words))
        fh.write("\n")

    print(f"generate_text: wrote {len(words)} words over {len(vocabulary)} vocabulary words "
          f"({base} each, +1 for the first {remainder}) to {outputs['output1']}")

nodes.name: split
nodes.description: The split function partitions the input text into N batches (N=3, the number of mapping functions). Reads the whole input text, tokenizes on whitespace, and writes N contiguous, near-equal-size batches (sizes differ by at most one word, words preserved in order; the first W mod N batches get one extra word), one ranked batch file per map instance (batch r goes to map rank r), each as whitespace-separated words. N is taken from the number of output batch files (default 3). Must be fully generalizable to any vocabulary size and word frequency: no word list is assumed.

outputs.name: batch_{rank}.txt
outputs.description: batch r of the text, for map rank r

nodes.code:
"""Split the MapReduce input text into N contiguous, near-equal word batches.

N is the number of output batch paths (one per map rank). Words are kept in order;
the first (W mod N) batches get one extra word. Works for any vocabulary.
"""


def main(inputs: dict, outputs: dict, params: dict) -> None:
    batch_paths = outputs["output1"]
    if isinstance(batch_paths, str):
        batch_paths = [batch_paths]
    batch_paths = list(batch_paths)
    n_batches = len(batch_paths)
    if n_batches == 0:
        raise ValueError("outputs['output1'] holds no batch paths; cannot split into 0 batches")

    with open(inputs["input1"], "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        words = fh.read().split()

    if not words:
        msg = f"input text {inputs['input1']} contains no words"
        print(f"split: ERROR {msg}")
        raise ValueError(msg)

    total = len(words)
    base, remainder = divmod(total, n_batches)

    start = 0
    for i, path in enumerate(batch_paths):
        size = base + (1 if i < remainder else 0)
        batch = words[start:start + size]
        start += size
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(" ".join(batch))
            fh.write("\n")
        print(f"split: batch {i + 1}/{n_batches}: {len(batch)} words -> {path}")

    if start != total:
        raise RuntimeError(f"split assigned {start} words, expected {total}")

    print(f"split: partitioned {total} words into {n_batches} batches "
          f"({base} each, +1 for the first {remainder})")

nodes.name: map
nodes.description: N parallel map functions (N=3) count how often each word occurs in their text chunk. Each ranked instance reads the batch matching its rank (params['rank']), tokenizes on whitespace, and writes its per-chunk word-count result Y_i as a JSON object mapping word -> count for that chunk. Must be fully generalizable to vocabularies of any size and frequency (no hard-coded words; every distinct word found is counted, case-sensitive, no normalization). An empty batch yields an empty object.

outputs.name: map_counts_{rank}.json
outputs.description: Y_i: word -> count within this batch

nodes.code:
"""MapReduce map step: count word occurrences in this rank's text batch.

Tokenizes on whitespace (case-sensitive, no normalization) and writes Y_i as a JSON
object mapping word -> count. Works for vocabularies of any size and frequency.
"""

import json
from collections import Counter


def main(inputs: dict, outputs: dict, params: dict) -> None:
    rank = params.get("rank")
    max_rank = params.get("max_rank")

    in_path = inputs["input1"]
    out_path = outputs["output1"]

    with open(in_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        words = fh.read().split()

    counts = Counter(words)
    # Sorted keys for deterministic output.
    result = {word: counts[word] for word in sorted(counts)}

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(result, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
        fh.write("\n")

    print(f"map: rank {rank}/{max_rank}: {len(words)} words, "
          f"{len(result)} distinct -> {out_path}")
    for word, count in result.items():
        print(f"map: rank {rank}: {word} = {count}")

nodes.name: shuffle
nodes.description: Shuffle flattens the resulting array Y_i from all N mappers (the list of every ranked map output) into a flat list of (word, partial count) pairs and groups them by word, so that each of the M reducers gets the partial counts for its respective word. The available workflow primitives necessitate this shuffle function, not relying on the array Y_i itself but flattening it to enable the desired level of parallelism in reduce. The set of distinct words is discovered from the map outputs and sorted lexicographically; word k (0-based, in sorted order) is assigned to reducer rank (k mod M) + 1, where M is the number of output partition files (the reduce step's rank count, 5). It writes exactly M ranked partition files (one per reducer rank), each a JSON object mapping each assigned word -> list of its partial counts from the mappers; a partition with no assigned words is an empty object. With M=5 distinct words each reducer gets exactly one word. Must be fully generalizable to vocabularies of any size and frequency (no hard-coded words).

outputs.name: partition_{rank}.json
outputs.description: words assigned to reducer rank r -> list of partial counts

nodes.code:
"""MapReduce shuffle step: flatten all mapper outputs Y_1..Y_N into (word, partial count)
pairs, group them by word, and partition the words across the M reducers.

Distinct words are sorted lexicographically; word k (0-based) goes to reducer rank
(k mod M) + 1. Each partition file is a JSON object word -> list of partial counts (in
mapper rank order). Works for vocabularies of any size and frequency.
"""

import json


def main(inputs: dict, outputs: dict, params: dict) -> None:
    in_paths = inputs["input1"]
    out_paths = outputs["output1"]

    if isinstance(in_paths, str):
        in_paths = [in_paths]
    if isinstance(out_paths, str):
        out_paths = [out_paths]

    if not in_paths:
        raise ValueError("shuffle: input1 (map outputs) holds no files")
    if not out_paths:
        raise ValueError("shuffle: output1 (reducer partitions) holds no paths")

    # Flatten Y_i into a list of (word, partial count) pairs.
    pairs = []
    for path in in_paths:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            counts = json.load(fh)
        if not isinstance(counts, dict):
            raise ValueError(f"shuffle: {path} is not a JSON object of word -> count")
        for word, count in counts.items():
            if isinstance(count, bool) or not isinstance(count, int):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"shuffle: {path}: count for {word!r} is not an integer: {count!r}")
            pairs.append((word, count))
        print(f"shuffle: read {len(counts)} words from {path}")

    # Group by word.
    grouped = {}
    for word, count in pairs:
        grouped.setdefault(word, []).append(count)

    m = len(out_paths)
    partitions = [{} for _ in range(m)]
    for k, word in enumerate(sorted(grouped)):
        partitions[k % m][word] = grouped[word]

    for r, (path, part) in enumerate(zip(out_paths, partitions), start=1):
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(part, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
            fh.write("\n")
        print(f"shuffle: partition {r}/{m}: {sorted(part)} -> {path}")

    print(f"shuffle: {len(pairs)} pairs, {len(grouped)} distinct words, "
          f"{m} partitions")

nodes.name: reduce
nodes.description: M reducers (M=5) count the total occurrences of their respective word in parallel, yielding Z_i. Each ranked instance reads the shuffled partition matching its rank (params['rank']), sums the list of partial counts for each word in it, and writes Z_i as a JSON object mapping word -> total occurrences (empty object if the partition is empty). Must be fully generalizable to vocabularies of any size and frequency (no hard-coded words; handles any number of words per partition).
nodes.code:
"""MapReduce reduce step: reducer rank i reads its shuffled partition (word -> list of
partial counts) and writes Z_i, a JSON object word -> total occurrences.

Works for vocabularies of any size and frequency; an empty partition yields {}.
"""

import json


def main(inputs: dict, outputs: dict, params: dict) -> None:
    rank = params.get("rank")
    max_rank = params.get("max_rank")
    in_path = inputs["input1"]
    out_path = outputs["output1"]

    with open(in_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        partition = json.load(fh)
    if not isinstance(partition, dict):
        raise ValueError(
            f"reduce[{rank}/{max_rank}]: {in_path} is not a JSON object of word -> counts")

    totals = {}
    for word, counts in partition.items():
        if isinstance(counts, bool) or isinstance(counts, int):
            counts = [counts]
        if not isinstance(counts, list):
            raise ValueError(
                f"reduce[{rank}/{max_rank}]: counts for {word!r} is not a list: {counts!r}")
        total = 0
        for c in counts:
            if isinstance(c, bool) or not isinstance(c, int):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"reduce[{rank}/{max_rank}]: partial count for {word!r} "
                    f"is not an integer: {c!r}")
            total += c
        totals[word] = total

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(totals, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
        fh.write("\n")

    print(f"reduce[{rank}/{max_rank}]: {len(totals)} words -> {totals} -> {out_path}")

assumptions: "each distributed evenly" -> exactly W/5 = 1000 occurrences per word; if W is not divisible, the first words get one extra each so the total is exactly W
"shuffled randomly" -> random shuffle with an optional seed parameter; unseeded by default, so each run's text differs (counts do not)
"partitions the input text into N batches" -> contiguous near-equal word batches (sizes differ by at most one), not split by lines or bytes
word tokenization -> split on whitespace, case-sensitive, no punctuation stripping

"M reducers ... their respective word" generalized -> distinct words sorted alphabetically, word k goes to reducer (k mod M)+1; with more words than reducers a reducer handles several, with fewer some get an empty partition
M is fixed by the reduce step's rank count (5) at deploy time; the reducer count does not change at run time with the vocabulary
presentation_assumptions: generated text -> one plain-text file, single-space separated, one line
intermediate and final results -> JSON objects mapping word -> count (map), word -> list of partial counts (shuffle), word -> total (reduce)
final output -> one file per reducer (word_total_1..5.json), no extra combined summary step
